user.text:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
Built the book tracker in Next.js. The home page shows currently reading and finished books, with a form to add a title, author, and optional notes. You can mark a book finished and open its shareable `/books/[id]` page to see its details and copy the link.

Books are saved in `data/books.json` so they survive a restart on a writable, persistent filesystem. Run it with `npm run dev`.

Verification passed: `npm test` (3 tests), `npm run build`, a local add/detail/finish flow, and `npm audit` (0 vulnerabilities). The smoke-test book was removed afterward.

A small personal book tracker built with Next.js. No accounts or database.

## Run locally

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Add a book with a title, author, and optional notes; it appears in **Currently reading**. Mark it finished to move it to **Finished books**. Open a book to see its details and copy its individual URL to share it.

Books are stored in `data/books.json`. The app creates the directory/file if missing, and writes changes to disk, so they survive a restart. Keep the app on a writable, persistent filesystem and back up that file if you want to keep your library. Ephemeral/serverless hosting will not retain the file across deployments or instances. This app is intended for a single local or self-hosted instance; it has no authentication.

## Checks

```sh
npm test
npm run build
```

# Reading Room

A small personal book tracker built with Next.js. No accounts or database.

## Run locally

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Add a book with a title, author, and optional notes; it appears in **Currently reading**. Mark it finished to move it to **Finished books**. Open a book to see its details and copy its individual URL to share it.

Books are stored in `data/books.json`. The app creates the directory/file if missing, and writes changes to disk, so they survive a restart. Keep the app on a writable, persistent filesystem and back up that file if you want to keep your library. Ephemeral/serverless hosting will not retain the file across deployments or instances. This app is intended for a single local or self-hosted instance; it has no authentication.

## Checks

```sh
npm test
npm run build
```
